rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Araf passage describes the worshipped idols as lifeless: they cannot create, help, hear, see, move, or do anything, in contrast with God's hearing and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وصف آلهتهم بأنها لا تسمع ولا تبصر ولا تتحرك ولا تقدر على شيء مما يدل على أنها ليس فيها شيء من الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Araf context gives no hint that the idols possess God's faculties, the predicates samiʿ and ʿalim can remain indefinite; nothing there calls for an implied denial of shared qualities.
rows.anchor: فوردت الصفتان بقوله: (سميع عليم) مورداً لم يتقدمه ما يوهم صلاحية شيء من ذلك لغيره تعالى مما عبدوه من دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Fussilat, the belief that God misses much and the human and jinn companions suggest rival capacities; definiteness signals perfect hearing and knowledge, while the separating pronoun restricts both to God.
rows.anchor: فجاء بالصفتين معرّفتين للدلالة على الكمال في الوصف، وجاء بضمير الفصل للدلالة على قصر هاتين الصفتين عليه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 2:15, God extends people in their own self-earned transgression; in 7:202, Satan extends them in fresh deviation, so the first noun is possessive and the second unqualified.
rows.anchor: فقد عرف (الطغيان) بالإضافة وعن (الغيّ) بأل، وذلك أنه أسند المد في آية البقرة إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites al-Kashshaf's explanation that the possessive form marks transgression as the people's own acquired wrongdoing, of which God is innocent; Satan's unqualified ghayy adds deviation to their existing error.
rows.anchor: والتمادي في الضلالة مما اقترفته أنفسهم واجترحته أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction wāw joins events without itself specifying their order or interval; context may make it ordered, but it does not explicitly require sequence.
rows.anchor: وأما الواو فكما ذكرنا لمطلق الجمع، أي: ليست للتريب وإنما هي لمجرد الاشتراك في الحدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa marks sequence with immediate succession, whereas the interval depends on the events being described.
rows.anchor: وأن الفاء تفيد الترتيب والتعقيب، و (ثم) تفيد الترتيب والتراخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks sequence with an interval; the amount of delay is relative to the events, such as pregnancy between marriage and birth.
rows.anchor: و (ثم) تفيد الترتيب والتراخي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the human creation sequence, fa joins death to burial because burial follows soon, while thumma marks the long delay from burial to resurrection.
rows.anchor: فجاء في (أقبره) بالفاء، لأن دفن الميت يكون بعد موته مباشرة وجاء بعده بـ (ثم) لأن النشور يتأخر عن الدفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first revival follows the original lifeless state without delay, so it takes fa; death and the second revival occur later, so they take thumma.
rows.anchor: لأن الإحياء الأول قد تعقب الموت بغير تراخي وأما الموت فقد تراخى عن الإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Abraham's account, fa links creation to guidance without delay, while thumma marks resurrection as delayed after death.
rows.anchor: فقد عطف في الآية الأولى بالفاء لتعقب بلا مهلة الهداية للخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in Abraham's statement that God heals him is the fa connecting the response to its condition, not a conjunction between sequential events.
rows.anchor: وأما الفاء في قوله: (فهو يشفينِ) فهي الرابطة للجواب وليست عاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Initial creation develops gradually until dust can receive life; resurrection follows God's call directly, without a gradual process, so the emergence clause needs no further thumma.
rows.anchor: هناك يكون خلق وتقدير وتدريج وتراخ حتى يصير التراب قابلاً للحياة فينفخ فيه روحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta-Ha uses fa because it has just described worldly punishment, making the warning immediate; al-Sajda uses wāw because its preceding judgment is deferred to Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فجاء بالفاء في (طه) لأنها تفيد التعقيب وجاء الواو في السجدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sajda adds min to mark the starting point among those destroyed, beginning with people nearest the Prophet's time; Ta-Ha omits it because Moses's people were much earlier.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بهلاك من هو أقرب إليه فجاء بـ (من) الدالة على ابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported explanation for placing al-ʿAziz before al-Hakim is that God is mighty, then exercises judgment.
rows.anchor: قالوا: لأنه عَزَّ فَحكَمَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Strength precedes might because being strong leads to being victorious and mighty.
rows.anchor: ومنه تقديم القوة على العزة لأنه قوي فعزّ أي غلب فالقوة أول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering in 4:69 follows merit: God precedes the Messenger, then prophets, truthful people, martyrs, and righteous people; the most excellent classes are also the smallest.
rows.anchor: فقدم الله على الرسول، ثم قدم السعداء من الخلق بحسب تفاضلهم، فبدأ بالأفضلين وهم النبيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is named first among the covenant-taking prophets because he is the most excellent of them.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالرسول لأنه أفضلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported proof that hearing is superior is that no prophet was deaf, though a prophet such as Jacob could become blind after losing his child.
rows.anchor: قالوا: لأن السمع أفضل. قالوا: والدليل على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author grounds hearing's priority in receiving revelation: a blind person can understand a message like a sighted person, but a deaf person cannot receive it as easily and is farther from understanding.
rows.anchor: فالأصم أنأى عن الفهم من الأعمى، ولذا كان من العميان علماء كبار بخلاف الصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reason for hearing before sight is its shorter range: hearing ordinarily suggests nearness, so God's promise to hear and see Moses and Aaron conveys closeness.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون تقديم السمع على البصر لسبب آخر عدا الأفضلية، وهو أن مدى السمع أقل من مدى الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves through escalating harm: insulting, carrying tales, withholding good, aggression, and finally athim as a comprehensive label for evil.
rows.anchor: ثم انتقل إلى مرتبة أبعد من الإيذاء، وهو أنه يمنع الخير عن الآخرين، وهذه مرتبة أبعد في الإيذاء مما تقدمها

rows.speaker: بدائع الفوائد
rows.claim: Bada'i al-Fawa'id explains that talebearing requires movement while backbiting does not, and that preventing good affects oneself before aggression reaches another.
rows.anchor: جاء في (بدائع الفوائد) : "وأما تقدم (هماز) على (مشاء بنميم) فالرتبة لأن المشي مرتب على القعود في المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In warnings and threats, hearing is placed before knowledge because hearing whispers and faint sounds feels nearer and makes the warning more forceful, although God's knowledge encompasses the near and far, seen and hidden.
rows.anchor: فإن مَنْ سمع حِسَكَ وخَفيّ صوتك أقرب إليك في العادة ممن يقال لك: إنه يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that hearing may precede knowledge because hearing is one of the means by which knowledge is acquired.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال: إن السمع من وسائل العلم فهو يسبقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness may precede mercy because safety comes before gain; Saba reverses the order because mercy is universal to creatures while forgiveness concerns only the morally responsible, making the general prior by rank.
rows.anchor: والسلامة مطلوبة قبل الغنيمة وإنما تأخرت في آية سبأ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The reported explanation for forehead, sides, then backs is a progression in rank: hoarders frowned at the poor, turned away when sharing a gathering, and finally turned their backs.
rows.anchor: قيل: لأنهم كانوا إذا أبصروا الفقير عبسوا وإذا ضمهم وإياه مجلس أزوروا عنه وتولوا بأركانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order in 2:125 rises from fewer to more: tawaf is confined to the Kaaba, retreat to mosques, and prayer to any pure place; each rakʿah has two prostrations, with some prostrations outside prayer.
rows.anchor: فالطائفون أقل من العاكفين لأن الطواف لا يكون إلا حول الكعبة. والعكوف يكون في المساجد عموماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the passage concerns the Sacred House, it begins with those closest to it, the circumambulators, then those worshipping in mosques, then those who face it in prayer across the earth.
rows.anchor: فالطائفون هم ألصق المذكورين بالبيت لأنهم يطوفون حوله، فبدأ بهم ثم تدرج إلى العاكفين

words: ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands in 22:77 expand from the less numerous act of bowing to prostration, broader worship of God, and finally doing good.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالركوع وهو أقل المذكورات، ثم السجود وهو أكثر، ثم عبادة الرب وهو أعم، ثم فعل الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is told first to perform qnut, the broadest worship, then the narrower acts of prostration and bowing, moving from general to specific.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالقنوت وهو عموم العبادة، ثم السجود وهو أقل وأخص، ثم الركوع وهو أقل وأخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers are mentioned before believers because they are more numerous, as 12:103 says most people will not believe.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالكفار لأنهم أكثر

words: ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُم مُّقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites al-Kashshaf's explanation that the order from wrongdoer to moderate to forerunner signals that wrongdoers predominate, moderates are fewer, and forerunners are fewer still.
rows.anchor: للإيذان بكثرة الفاسقين وغلبتهم وأن المقتصدين قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the rarity of the forerunners to 56:13–14, which calls them many among earlier generations and few among later ones.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ندرتهم وقلة وجودهم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported explanation for naming male thieves before female thieves is that theft is more common among men.
rows.anchor: قدم السارق على السارقة لأن السرقة في الذكور أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported explanation for naming the female fornicator first is that fornication is more common among women.
rows.anchor: وقدم الزانية على الزاني في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: حاشية ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir says the woman is foregrounded in the legal discussion because the conduct begins through her display, suggestive looks, enticement, and speech.
rows.anchor: وجاء في حاشية ابن المنير على "الكشاف" قوله: "وقدم الزانية على الزاني والسبب فيه أن الكلام الأول في حكم الزنى

rows.speaker: حاشية ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munir also argues that the mischief of fornication is more fully realized in relation to the woman.
rows.anchor: لأن مفسدته تتحقق بالإضافة إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Order can also follow other considerations suited to a passage, so a word may come first in one context and later in another.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون التقديم لملاحظ أخرى تتناسب مع السياق فنراه يقدم لفظة في موضع ويؤخرها في موضع آخر
